definitions.explanation: Money paid regularly to an employee for their work.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}は{毎月|まいつき}25{日|にち}に{出|で}ます。
examples.english: Salary is paid on the 25th of every month.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}が{上|あ}がりました。
{給料|きゅうりょう}だけでは{生活|せいかつ}が{大変|たいへん}です。
examples.english: It's hard to live on just my salary.

examples.japanese: {給料|きゅうりょう}から{税金|ぜいきん}が{引|ひ}かれます。
examples.english: Taxes are deducted from the salary.

examples.japanese: {転職|てんしょく}したら{給料|きゅうりょう}は{下|さ}がりましたが、{仕事|しごと}は{楽|らく}になりました。
examples.english: My salary went down when I changed jobs, but the work became easier.

notes:
{給料|きゅうりょう} is the general term for salary or wages paid to employees.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {給料|きゅうりょう}をもらう: to receive a salary
- {給料|きゅうりょう}が{上|あ}がる: salary goes up
- {給料|きゅうりょう}が{下|さ}がる: salary goes down
- {給料|きゅうりょう}から{引|ひ}かれる: to be deducted from salary

RELATED TERMS:
- {月給|げっきゅう}: monthly salary
- {年収|ねんしゅう}: annual income
- {時給|じきゅう}: hourly wage
- {給料日|きゅうりょうび}: payday
- {手取|てど}り: take-home pay (after deductions)
- {額面|がくめん}: gross salary (before deductions)

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, many companies pay salaries on the 25th of each month. The expression {給料日前|きゅうりょうびまえ} (before payday) often implies being short on money.
